case_title: State of Himachal Pradesh v. Raj Kumar
accused_victim_relationship: Relative (brother-in-law of the deceased); prior dispute, as the accused frequently quarrelled with and assaulted her
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302; s.201 read with s.34
evidence_type: Circumstantial (principal); medical autopsy evidence; testimony of son (PW-1) on the beating and the accused taking the victim away; motive evidence of PW-15
confession: Investigation recorded a confession on 27.08.2007 leading to recovery of a lady shirt; the Court did not rely on it in its reasoning
aggravating_circumstances: Accused beat the deceased and took her away; did not report her missing; no explanation for her death; prior assault on her and frequent quarrels
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 IPC and s.201 read with s.34 IPC; sentenced to life imprisonment
high_court_outcome: Appeal allowed; conviction and life sentence set aside (accused acquitted)
neutral_facts: The victim, a woman whose husband had died about eleven years earlier, lived in a joint family house with her son, her daughter and the accused, her brother-in-law. On the evening of 23 August 2007, the accused came to the house in a drunken state, abused the victim and her children and threatened to kill them. An elderly woman in the house took the son into an adjoining room and bolted it from outside, and sent the daughter to the house of the victim's maternal uncle. From the room's window, the son heard the victim crying out and saw the accused taking her towards the house of another person. Hours later, the accused opened the door and told the son that the victim had run away, and told him to tell the maternal uncle the same. Under threat from the accused and another person, the son told the uncle so. The uncle came to the house in the early hours of 24 August, and the son and uncle reported the victim missing at the police station. On 25 August the uncle received a call that the victim's body was hanging from a tree in a forest. The body was found hanging from a pine branch, a plastic rope tied around the neck. The autopsy surgeon found death due to haemorrhagic shock from a ruptured spleen, with anti-mortem injuries suggesting gagging, and found hanging was after death. The accused was taken into custody on 25 August. His confession on 27 August led to recovery of a lady's shirt from a room under construction. The sister-in-law testified that the victim had told her of ill-treatment by the accused, including an earlier beating and a compromise, and that the accused was a chronic drunkard. The accused did not report the victim missing to the police and gave no explanation for her death.
physical_harm: Death of the victim; haemorrhagic shock from ruptured spleen and anti-mortem injuries suggesting gagging; hanging was post-mortem
motive: Accepted by the Court on PW-15's evidence: frequent quarrels and assaults on the deceased, a land dispute over property Swami wanted to give to her, and greed for a fixed deposit of Rs.1,20,000 due to the deceased
key_evidence_accepted: PW-1's evidence of the beating and the accused taking the victim away; PW-15's motive evidence; PW-24's autopsy finding of homicide; the accused's failure to report her missing; his absence of explanation; the last-seen circumstance; FSL finding of no poison
witness_credibility: PW-1 (son) found cogent, natural and trustworthy; trial court's view that he was trustworthy upheld; High Court wrongly doubted him on alleged improvements. Omission of two names in his first statement explained by trauma and fear
post_offence_conduct: Told the son the victim had run away; did not report her missing to police or the maternal uncle; gave no explanation for her death
custody_duration: Not stated (taken into custody on 25.08.2007; duration not given)
trial_duration: offence: 23.08.2007; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 19.08.2014; Supreme Court: 08.01.2018
legal_representation: For the State (appellant): D. K. Thakur, AAG, Shariq Ahmed, Varinder Kumar Sharma, Advs. For the accused (respondent): Jose Abraham, Ruchir Batra, Advs.
investigation_status: FIR No.250 of 2007 registered; investigation completed; chargesheet filed; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.302 and s.201 r/w s.34 IPC, life imprisonment. High Court: appeal allowed, conviction set aside. Supreme Court: State's appeal allowed, conviction and life sentence affirmed
defence_argument: Suggested that the deceased consumed poison and committed suicide; the Court rejected this as FSL found no poison. Submissions before the Supreme Court not recorded
legal_principle_applied: Circumstantial evidence test (cogent proof, conclusive circumstances, complete chain, consistent only with guilt); s.106 Evidence Act burden on the inmate to explain; last-seen-together circumstance
precedent_relied_upon: Trimukh Maroti Kirkan v. State of Maharashtra (2006) 10 SCC 681; State of Rajasthan v. Kashi Ram (2006) 12 SCC 254; Ganesh Lal v. State of Rajasthan (2002) 1 SCC 731; State of Maharashtra v. Suresh (2000) 1 SCC 471; State of Tamil Nadu v. Rajendran (1999) 8 SCC 679
judicial_aggravating_factors: Accused's failure to explain the victim's death and his failure to report her missing, treated as strong militating circumstances
other_sentence_order: Direction that the respondent be taken into custody to serve the remaining sentence
